title: POC scoping: LumaHealth Quality Eval Plan
summary: AE+SE scoped POC success criteria and drafted a quality evaluation plan: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination & format checks, scoring rubric, and timelines. Agreed on workload sizing (10k monthly inference, 5k golden prompts), baseline benchmarks and pilot timeline. Next: Redwood to share eval template, benchmark harness, and sample results; customer to provide 200 golden prompts and access to sample dataset.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-22 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Recorder: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Nate Carter (Redwood AE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Aisha Khan (LumaHealth), Mark Liu (LumaHealth), Ben Torres (LumaHealth)
---
[00:00] Nate: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time. We sent a brief agenda - POC success criteria, workload sizing, bench plan, and then the quality eval approach.
[00:14] Dr. Khan: Yep, thanks Nate. Quick note, we're short on time later today so want to make sure we lock the eval plan and who owns the prompts.
[00:22] Sofia: Great, we'll go fast. High level - for Luma we recommend a two-week benchmark then a four-week pilot where we run the golden prompts + regression harness.
[00:34] Mark: Sounds reasonable. Our core success criteria are accuracy on triage suggestions, <10% hallucination, and sub-150ms median token latency for 95% of requests. Cost target is under $0.45 per 1k tokens during pilot.
[00:50] Nate: Good, putting that down as success criteria. Sofia, can you talk about workload sizing?
[00:57] Sofia: Sure. From what you told us you expect a bursty pattern, roughly 10k requests per month, average prompt length ~120 tokens, response 80 tokens. For the POC we'll recommend simulating 2k/day for peak testing and a steady 300/day baseline. That maps to roughly 1.2M tokens/month. For dedicated vs hosted tradeoff - hosted is easiest for fast start but Dedicated gives more predictable latencies during spikes.
[01:28] Ben: We definitely care about predictable latency; we have internal SLAs to keep follow-ups within X. Also need to confirm data residency, since some PHI may be in payloads.
[01:36] Nate: Right - we'll outline options. Private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS, both support SOC 2 controls. We'll send the security pack.
[01:46] Dr. Khan: Okay. On benchmarks - what exactly will you measure during the two-week baseline?
[01:52] Sofia: We'll run (1) latency P95/P99, (2) throughput at various concurrency levels, (3) accuracy metrics against golden prompts, (4) hallucination checks, (5) output format conformance. We use a harness that can replay your request traces or synthetic load.
[02:12] Mark: For accuracy scoring - what rubric do you use? Precision/recall or BLEU-ish?
[02:17] Sofia: We do a hybrid. For structured outputs (JSON fields) we use exact-match / regex checks and weighted field scoring. For free text triage suggestions we use a scored rubric - relevance (0-3), correctness (0-3), hallucination flag (0/1) - then normalize to a 100-point scale. We'll share the scoring sheet.
[02:36] [crosstalk] Ben: And regression tests?
[02:38] Sofia: Regression harness runs your golden set (we recommend 200-500 golden prompts) each commit, plus a weekly random sample. If a regression exceeds threshold - say a 5-point drop on the normalized score or hallucination increase >3% - we alert and can pin a rollback model.
[02:58] Dr. Khan: How do you detect hallucinations automatically? That's been a pain for us.
[03:03] Sofia: We combine heuristics and a reference-based check. Heuristics include unexpected entity injection, out-of-scope claims, and format divergence. Reference-based is exactness against ground-truth where available. For free text we run a lightweight NLI/verification model to flag high-risk outputs, then sample for human review. It's not perfect - we'll show you examples.
[03:30] Nate: Important note - transcription: when we say NLI here we mean a fast verifier, not a full human evaluation. For POC we'll do automated gating + 10% manual review.
[03:42] Mark: That 10% manual, who will do it? Our team or Redwood?
[03:46] Nate: We can do joint reviews for the pilot - Redwood will sample and annotate, your SMEs confirm. We'll budget 4-6 hours/week for review during the pilot.
[03:58] Ben: About golden prompts - we can supply 200 to start, but want guidance on coverage.
[04:03] Sofia: Good. We'll provide a template with categories: triage happy path, edge cases, PHI-handling prompts, multi-turn follow ups, and format enforcement prompts. Aim for at least 20 prompts per category. That gives coverage across intents.
[04:22] Dr. Khan: And regression tests should include format checks - we need strict JSON outputs for downstream ingestion.
[04:28] Sofia: Yes, we'll include JSON schema validation as a hard pass/fail in the harness. If schema fails, output marked as failed regardless of textual score.
[04:38] Mark: For scoring approach - you mentioned weighted fields. Can we customize weights? For us triage correctness > format.
[04:45] Sofia: Absolutely - weights are configurable in the eval sheet. We'll propose default weights, and you can tune them during week one of pilot.
[04:54] Nate: Timeline proposal: Week 0 - kickoff + data & access; Week 1-2 - baseline benchmarks & initial tuning; Week 3-6 - pilot run with golden prompts and regression harness; Week 7 - review & decision. Sound OK?
[05:09] Dr. Khan: That aligns with our timing. We want go/no-go by mid-June.
[05:14] Nate: Good. On tooling - we'll share the bench harness repo and a redwood-runner script that can run locally or in your VPC.
[05:24] Ben: Regarding cost measurement - can the harness give per-route token breakdowns and cost estimates?
[05:30] Sofia: Yes, the harness outputs token counts, per-request latency, and modeled cost given per-token rates. We'll map that to your expected monthly usage to show P95 cost.
[05:42] Mark: Any gotchas on quantization or model variants causing regressions? We saw differences between fp16 and int8 outputs before.
[05:49] Sofia: Good point. We'll include model-variant comparison tests in the regression matrix. If quantization introduces formatting/accuracy regressions beyond thresholds we recommend either pinning the non-quantized model for critical routes or applying a custom quant profile.
[06:03] Dr. Khan: Security checklist: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs - we need the PDF.
[06:09] Nate: We'll attach the security pack and the SOC 2 report when we send follow-ups. Also include SSO guide and VPC deployment checklist.
[06:17] Mark: Who owns the benchmark infra cost?
[06:20] Nate: Redwood covers initial bench runs for the POC. If you want extended dedicated infra we can quote for Dedicated or bring-your-own infra options.
[06:29] Ben: Good. One more on evaluation: how do we treat multi-turn context? Some of our flows depend on preserved KV cache across calls.
[06:36] Sofia: The harness can replay multi-turn sessions with KV state. We'll instrument for context window behavior and cache hit rates. We'll also report token savings from prefix caching.
[06:48] Dr. Khan: Ok let's walk through concrete deliverables and owners.
[06:52] Nate: I'll type these into the notes - deliverables: Redwood to share eval template, bench harness repo, sample run results. Luma to provide 200 golden prompts and a sample dataset (anonymized) and test accounts. Redwood to run baseline.
[07:07] Mark: Timeline for docs?
[07:09] Nate: I'll send the package by Friday 2026-04-24. Sofia will run initial baseline the following week.
[07:15] Sofia: Yup, plan is to have baseline run 04/27-05/10 and share report 05/11.
[07:22] Ben: We'll collect golden prompts and aim to deliver by 04/28.
[07:26] Dr. Khan: Great. Any other risks?
[07:28] Sofia: Biggest risks: hallucination thresholds not being reliable for free text, and unexpected schema failures with quantized models. Mitigations: sample-based human review and model pinning.
[07:40] Nate: Alright, quick recap and next steps.
[07:42] Nate: 1) Redwood to send eval template, security pack, and bench harness link by 04/24. 2) Luma to provide 200 golden prompts + sample dataset by 04/28. 3) Redwood to run baseline 04/27-05/10 and share report 05/11. 4) Joint pilot 05/11-06/07. 5) Final decision mid-June.
[07:58] Mark: Thanks everyone.
[08:00] Dr. Khan: Thanks, speak soon.
---
